text: Siobhan drove an hour in the rain to bring me soup when I was sick. Didn't even come in, just left it on the step with a note.
Thankful for my body today. It carried me up the mountain even though I doubted it.
The nurses on ward 7 were so kind to Dad tonight. One stayed past her shift to sit with him.
Someone paid for my coffee in the queue. Tiny thing. Changed my whole morning.
Rereading the messages everyone sent after the surgery. I didn't realise how many people care.
Mr. Achebe let me pay the rent late without any fuss. I'll remember that.
Grateful list: warm bed, a job I mostly like, Ollie making me laugh at breakfast, the smell of rain.
My therapist, Dana, said 'you did the hard thing'. I'm so thankful I found her.
Neighbours dug our car out of the snow before we were even awake.
Called Aunty Funmi to thank her for paying my exam fees years ago. She'd forgotten. I never will.
Lost my wallet on the train and a stranger posted it back with every card and the cash still in it. Faith in people: restored.
Thank you, coffee. Thank you, quiet Saturday. Thank you, whoever invented the electric blanket.
Hyejin covered my shift so I could see my son's recital. I owe her big.
Mum and Dad helped with the deposit. I know it was a stretch for them. I keep looking at the keys and thinking of them.
A year sober today. Grateful for the meetings, for Jim my sponsor, and for whoever I was a year ago who decided to try.
Feeling lucky. Healthy family, roof over our heads. Not everyone has that.
Professor Lindqvist wrote me the strongest reference I've ever seen. I teared up reading it.
Bad day but Aarav sat with me on the phone for an hour and didn't try to fix it. Just listened. That's a friend.
The village rallied after the fire. Clothes, food, a place to sleep. I don't know how to repay this.
My manager noticed I was struggling and gave me the week off, paid. No questions.
Thankful for slow mornings and the way the light comes through the kitchen blinds.
Kai fixed my laptop for free and refused to take money. Bought him a pizza instead. He accepted that.
I was so scared about the delivery and the midwife, Precious, was a rock. I'll name a plant after her. Maybe the baby.
Appreciating my old school friends tonight. Twenty years and we still show up for each other.
So grateful the test came back negative. Grateful for the doctor who caught it early. Grateful, grateful, grateful.
Gran left me her sewing machine. Every time I use it I feel her hands on mine.
The bus driver waited when he saw me running. Made the connection with a minute to spare.
Thank you note to myself: you got through a hard month. You didn't quit.
Rashid translated everything for Mum at the hospital so she wasn't lost. He stayed four hours.
Grateful for the library card. Free books, free wifi, free warmth.
The team threw me a surprise send-off. Speeches, a card everyone signed, Wendy cried. I didn't know I mattered this much here.
My partner took the night feeds all week so I could sleep. Feel human again. Love him so much.
Thankful that the storm missed us. Thinking of the people on the coast who weren't so lucky.
Coach Brennan stayed after training to help me with my serve. Every week, for free. Legend.
Got through the interview because Leon spent all weekend doing mock questions with me.
So much gratitude for this little flat. Small, damp in the corners, but mine and safe.
A kid at the park helped me find my glasses in the grass. Wouldn't take the reward. Just said 'have a nice day'.
Dad called just to say he's proud of me. He never says that. I'm holding on to it.
The food bank volunteers didn't make me feel ashamed. They chatted like it was normal. It meant everything.
Tamsin and Freddie looked after the dog for two weeks and sent daily photos. He's clearly been spoiled.
Thankful my brother answered at 3am. I needed a voice.
Our elderly neighbour, Mrs. Kowalski, brought pierogi for the whole street after the power cut.
Grateful for second chances. The firm hired me back after I left on bad terms.
The surgeon, Mr. Adebayo, explained everything slowly and drew me a diagram. I felt like a person not a case number.
I appreciate this ordinary life more since the accident. Even the boring parts.
Zainab dropped off a lasagne and a pile of library books when she heard about the breakup. She didn't ask any questions.
Thankful for headphones, for trains that run on time, for the sandwich lady who knows my order.
My students made me a card for my last day. 'You made maths not scary.' Kept it in my coat pocket all evening.
Pastor Mensah visited Grandma every week while she was sick. Thanked him today at the service.
So thankful for Wi-Fi calls. Saw my niece take her first steps from 4,000 miles away.
Thank god for the emergency plumber who came at midnight. Bless that man.
Feeling grateful but also guilty that Mum gave up so much so I could study here.
Sundar spotted the mistake in my report before it went to the client. Saved my skin.
The cleaner at the station, Dolores, always says good morning like she means it. I told her today how much it helps.
Thankful for this body that is healing, slowly, stubbornly.
Isaac taught me to drive with endless patience, even when I stalled at the same junction eight times.
Everyone at the shelter knew Ruby by name when I went to adopt her. Grateful for the people who took care of her first.
Grateful to be here. Plain as that. Some years I wasn't sure I would be.
Esme sent a box of my favourite snacks from home. Ate half of them at the kitchen counter. Felt so loved.
Deeply thankful to the stranger who stopped and called the ambulance when I fainted. I never got his name.
My landlady gave us her old sofa when ours broke. 'Better than the dump,' she said. It's lovely.
Thankful for Thursday dinners with Arjun and Meera. Same curry place for six years.
The interpreter at the asylum hearing made sure every word I said was heard. I hugged her after.
Grateful that the fever broke overnight. She's watching cartoons and asking for toast.
Big thank you to past me for meal-prepping on Sunday. Present me is very tired.
Brigitte read every page of my draft and left notes in green pen. Kindest edit I've ever had.
For the first time I'm grateful for the hard year. I learned who stays.
Thank you to the bakery that gives away its leftover bread. Ate like a king this week.
Abuelo held my face and said 'mi orgullo'. I'm grateful I got to hear that before he goes.
Grateful for good friends, cold beer, and the fact that the barbecue didn't set anything on fire.
